name: Low-tier routing for single-file leaf beads and test-only beads
hypothesis: Leaf beads touching only 1 file with low-complexity signals AND test-only beads regardless of file count succeed on low tier (haiku for Claude, gpt-5.3-codex-spark for Codex) at >=90% first-pass rate, reducing per-bead cost by ~60% for qualifying beads. Provider split ratio is unchanged — the router selects the provider, then the low tier maps to each provider's cheapest model.
change: In isLowComplexity(), return true immediately for IsTestOnlyBead() beads (bypassing signal counting). Other beads still use the existing >=2 signal threshold (leaf + single file + tdd:false etc.). SelectTier() returns TierLow, which the router dispatches to haiku (Claude) or codex-spark (Codex) based on the existing provider ratio.
measurement: Track success rate and cost of low-tier beads over 30 iterations. Success threshold: >=90% first-pass success rate. Cost threshold: >=50% reduction vs medium-tier baseline for qualifying beads.
risk: Medium. Haiku may fail on beads that appear simple but have subtle cross-file dependencies, increasing retries and negating cost savings. Test-only beads may require understanding complex package internals. Mitigation: escalation chain (haiku -> sonnet -> opus) catches failures; validation phase catches compilation errors; review phase catches weak tests.
study_summary: Extension 1 (2026-02-20): Routing bug fixed (process.go now uses escalation.SelectModel). Extension 2 (2026-02-21): 35 low-tier data points collected. Haiku: 20/20 actual builds succeeded (100% first-pass, exceeds >=90% threshold). 8 zero-duration haiku 'failures' are scope gate rejections, not model failures — the gate is working correctly. Codex-spark: 5/6 successes (83%), one failure retried successfully. Cost data for haiku was $0 due to a MergeCostData bug (fixed in c15ba8c3, Feb 15); a regression test added. Going forward, haiku cost will be tracked correctly. Cost reduction vs baseline not yet measurable for haiku (historical $0 entries are artifacts). Codex-spark avg ~$1.57/success vs $1.72 baseline (~9% savings, below 50% target but small sample). Continuing to accumulate clean cost data.
